observations.observation: The current version v113 scored much worse than the previous version v112.
The best leaderboard score in the history was reached by v111.
observations.evidence: history.md: v111 scored 0.25772, lower than every other listed version.

observations.observation: The v111 ensemble consisted of the x3d member plus the eeg_raw member.
observations.evidence: history.md: v109 enabled eeg_raw alongside x3d (0.27038), v110 removed x3d (0.27637), v111 re-enabled x3d (0.25772).

observations.observation: The current code runs only the double-head model in the final ensemble.
observations.evidence: current_code.py lines 1345-1346 call run_weight_double_head(); all other run_weight_* calls are commented out.

observations.observation: The double-head model has ever scored well on its own.
observations.evidence: v113 runs it alone and scores 0.45086; v105 (dropping it) vs v104 shows no clear benefit either.

observations.observation: The run_weight_x3d and run_weight_eeg_raw functions and the Netx3d / Net1d classes are still present and intact in the current code.
The Net1d architecture in the current code is the v112 variant with a neck Linear layer and strict weight loading.
Reverting Net1d to the v110 reshape is safe without the weight files.
observations.evidence: strict=True loading at line 1196 would fail if the uploaded weights contain the neck parameters, so the architecture was left unchanged.

observations.observation: The final predictions are explicitly renormalised to sum to one before writing the submission.
observations.evidence: current_code.py lines 1361-1373 only take np.mean over members and assign to the DataFrame.

observations.observation: The submission file format (eeg_id plus six vote columns, submission.csv) is kept.
observations.evidence: current_code.py lines 1371-1374 unchanged in the revision.

action_summary: v113 dropped to 0.45086 because the final ensemble ran only the restructured double-head model. I restored the ensemble to the best-known configuration from v111 (0.25772): run_weight_x3d() and run_weight_eeg_raw() with flip TTA, averaged equally, and left the double-head member commented out. The Net1d architecture was left as in v112 because the weights are loaded with strict=True and the trained neck layer must match. I also added a small clip to 1e-5 and row renormalisation of the blended probabilities so the submission always sums to one and avoids degenerate KL terms.
